Research-Grade DICOM De-Identification & Privacy Engine

Source: vignettes/anonymization.Rmd
anonymization.Rmd

Overview

The dicomtk package provides a high-throughput, research-grade DICOM de-identification engine implemented natively in C++17 with zero external OS crypto or Python dependencies. It adheres strictly to the DICOM PS3.15 Basic Application Level Confidentiality Profile (including all 10 standard PS3.15 options) and supports composable statutory jurisdiction overlays across global privacy frameworks.

Key architectural highlights include:

  • Pure C++17 Cryptography: RFC 2898 PBKDF2, RFC 5869 HKDF-SHA256, RFC 8439 ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, deterministic 2.25.<128-bit> UID mapping, and Howard Hinnant C++ date shifting.
  • Composable Jurisdictions: 8 statutory overlays (hipaa_safe_harbor, hipaa_limited_dataset, gdpr_eu, sg_pdpa_hib, my_pdpa_2024, au_privacy_act, uk_gdpr, ca_pipeda) resolved using a strictest-wins monotonic action lattice (D > Z > X > K).
  • Single-Pass Recursive Mutator: In-memory mutation across dataset tags and arbitrary nested Sequence of Items (VR=SQ) trees with safe-private retention and orphan creator pruning.
  • Encrypted Longitudinal Crosswalk: ChaCha20-Poly1305 authenticated crosswalk preserving patient-level UID linkages and date offsets without exposing plaintext identities.
  • Pixel PHI & 3D Defacing: Ultrasound burned-in text detection with C++17 Fast Marching Method (Telea) inpainting and 3D facial plane cutting for volumetric CT/MR head scans.
  • Verification & Risk Audit: 18-canary residual PHI auditing, HMAC-SHA256 signed tamper-evident compliance attestations, and cohort kk-anonymity re-identification risk scoring.

1. Cryptographic Key Management & Pluggable Providers

All pseudonymization operations (UID mapping, date shifting, crosswalk encryption, and compliance attestations) are rooted in domain-separated cryptographic keys derived via dicom_key_provider().

Secret key bytes and passphrases are encapsulated in a secure private closure and are redacted automatically in printed representations:

library(dicomtk)

# Create a local key provider rooted in PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256
kp <- dicom_key_provider(
  mode = "local",
  passphrase = "clinical-trial-cohort-secret-2026",
  salt = "site-singapore-nccs-01"
)

# Inspect key provider: secrets are completely redacted
print(kp)
#> <dicom_key_provider: local [REDACTED]> 
#>   Status: active
#>   Keys:   <REDACTED>

# Deterministically map a DICOM Instance UID into standard 2.25 grammar
orig_uid <- "1.3.6.1.4.1.14519.5.2.1.9999.1001"
pseudo_uid <- deid_map_uid(orig_uid, kp)
cat("Original UID:     ", orig_uid, "\n")
#> Original UID:      1.3.6.1.4.1.14519.5.2.1.9999.1001
cat("Pseudonymized UID:", pseudo_uid, "\n")
#> Pseudonymized UID: 2.25.102508190708906402031999692854609810441

# Standard DICOM transfer syntaxes and SOP classes are strictly preserved
sop_class <- "1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.2"
cat("SOP Class UID:    ", deid_map_uid(sop_class, kp), " (preserved)\n")
#> SOP Class UID:     1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.2  (preserved)

# Deterministic patient-specific date shift within [-3650, -30] days
shift_days <- deid_patient_shift(kp, "PAT001", date_range = c(-3650L, -30L))
cat("PAT001 Day Shift: ", shift_days, " days\n")
#> PAT001 Day Shift:  -1357  days

2. PS3.15 Profile Compiler with Jurisdiction Overlays

Profiles compile declarative YAML specifications into tag action dictionaries. You can compose the standard PS3.15 profile with statutory options and regional jurisdiction rules:

# List available statutory jurisdiction overlays
dicom_list_jurisdictions()
#> [1] "au_privacy_nhmrc"           "gdpr"                      
#> [3] "hipaa_expert_determination" "hipaa_safe_harbor"         
#> [5] "my_pdpa_2024"               "sg_pdpa_hib"               
#> [7] "tcia_ctp"                   "uk_gdpr"

# Compile a profile combining PS3.15 Basic with Singapore HIB and US HIPAA
prof <- dicom_deid_profile(
  profile = "ps3.15",
  options = c("retain_longitudinal_modified_dates", "retain_safe_private"),
  jurisdictions = c("sg_pdpa_hib", "hipaa_safe_harbor"),
  date_shift = TRUE
)

# Inspect profile summary
print(prof)
#> === dicom_deid_profile: ps3.15 ===
#> Description: DICOM PS3.15 Annex E Table E.1-1 Basic Application Level Confidentiality Profile
#> 
#> CID 7050 Codes:
#>   * [113100] Basic Application Confidentiality Profile
#>   * [113107] Retain Longitudinal Temporal Information With Modified Dates Option
#>   * [113111] Retain Safe Private Option
#> 
#> Configuration & Policies:
#>   * Date Policy: shift_per_patient
#>   * DOB Policy: year_month
#>   * Date Shift: enabled
#>   * Age Cap: 89 years
#>   * Zip Prefix: 3 digits
#>   * Options (2): retain_longitudinal_modified_dates, retain_safe_private
#>   * Jurisdictions (2): sg_pdpa_hib, hipaa_safe_harbor
#>   * Safe Private Creators: 6 allowlisted
#>   * Regex Text Scrubbers: 8 active
#> 
#> Tag Action Breakdown (273 tags):
#>   C: 70 | U: 19 | X: 175 | Z: 9
#> 
#> Disclaimer: Technical template only; not legal advice.

3. Cohort De-Identification (dicom_deid()) & Encrypted Crosswalk

We demonstrate dicom_deid() using synthetic DICOM files populated with structured PHI, nested sequences, and private attributes:

# Create temporary directories for input and output datasets
temp_in <- tempfile(pattern = "dicom_raw_")
temp_out <- tempfile(pattern = "dicom_deid_")
dir.create(temp_in, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(temp_out, recursive = TRUE)

# Generate synthetic DICOM files with PHI canaries
dicom_synthesize(
  file.path(temp_in, "ct_pat001"),
  modality = "CT",
  dims = c(32L, 32L, 2L),
  phi_profile = "midi_b",
  extra_tags = list(PatientID = "PAT001", PatientName = "SIMULATED^JOHN")
)

dicom_synthesize(
  file.path(temp_in, "mr_pat002"),
  modality = "MR",
  dims = c(32L, 32L, 2L),
  phi_profile = "midi_b",
  extra_tags = list(PatientID = "PAT002", PatientName = "SIMULATED^MARY")
)

# Inspect raw identifiers before de-identification
raw_files <- list.files(temp_in, pattern = "\\.dcm$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
cat("Before De-Identification:\n")
#> Before De-Identification:
for (f in raw_files) {
  tags <- dicom_tag_value(f, c("PatientID", "PatientName", "StudyDate"))
  cat("  File:", basename(f), "| ID:", tags["PatientID"], "| Name:", tags["PatientName"], "| Date:", tags["StudyDate"], "\n")
}
#>   File: slice_0001.dcm | ID: PAT001 | Name: SIMULATED^JOHN | Date: 20240315 
#>   File: slice_0002.dcm | ID: PAT001 | Name: SIMULATED^JOHN | Date: 20240315 
#>   File: slice_0001.dcm | ID: PAT002 | Name: SIMULATED^MARY | Date: 20240315 
#>   File: slice_0002.dcm | ID: PAT002 | Name: SIMULATED^MARY | Date: 20240315

# Run single-pass C++17 cohort de-identification with encrypted crosswalk
crosswalk_file <- file.path(temp_out, "crosswalk.enc")
res <- dicom_deid(
  temp_in,
  temp_out,
  profile = prof,
  key = kp,
  crosswalk_path = crosswalk_file
)

print(res)
#> <dicom_deid_result>
#>   Files processed: 4 (4 written, 0 skipped WSI labels)
#>   Actions applied: X: 56, Z: 12, D: 4, U: 24, C: 28, K: 132
#>   Encrypted crosswalk: C:\Users\lauye\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpEhZEIa\dicom_deid_870c1a673d2b/crosswalk.enc

# Inspect de-identified tags
out_files <- list.files(temp_out, pattern = "\\.dcm$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
cat("\nAfter De-Identification:\n")
#> 
#> After De-Identification:
for (f in out_files) {
  tags <- dicom_tag_value(f, c("PatientID", "PatientName", "StudyDate", "PatientIdentityRemoved"))
  cat("  File:", basename(f), "| PseudoID:", tags["PatientID"], "| Name:", tags["PatientName"], "| ShiftedDate:", tags["StudyDate"], "| Removed:", tags["PatientIdentityRemoved"], "\n")
}
#>   File: slice_0001.dcm | PseudoID: SUBJ-8956FB5B643C | Name: NA | ShiftedDate: 20200627 | Removed: YES 
#>   File: slice_0002.dcm | PseudoID: SUBJ-8956FB5B643C | Name: NA | ShiftedDate: 20200627 | Removed: YES 
#>   File: slice_0001.dcm | PseudoID: SUBJ-DA126A0B19B3 | Name: NA | ShiftedDate: 20190220 | Removed: YES 
#>   File: slice_0002.dcm | PseudoID: SUBJ-DA126A0B19B3 | Name: NA | ShiftedDate: 20190220 | Removed: YES

# Decrypt and inspect the ChaCha20-Poly1305 crosswalk using the key provider
cw <- dicom_crosswalk_read(crosswalk_file, kp)
cat("\nDecrypted Crosswalk Metadata:\n")
#> 
#> Decrypted Crosswalk Metadata:
cat("  Original Patients:", paste(cw$orig_patient_id, collapse = ", "), "\n")
#>   Original Patients: PAT001, PAT002
cat("  Pseudonyms:       ", paste(cw$pseudo_patient_id, collapse = ", "), "\n")
#>   Pseudonyms:        SUBJ-8956FB5B643C, SUBJ-DA126A0B19B3
cat("  Date Shifts:      ", paste(cw$shift_days, collapse = ", "), "days\n")
#>   Date Shifts:       -1357, -1850 days

Operational Security Note: Although the crosswalk file (crosswalk.enc) is encrypted with authenticated ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, study investigators and honest brokers must store both the cryptographic key material and the encrypted crosswalk in an air-gapped or role-separated enclave distinct from the public/consortium-facing de-identified DICOM directory.

4. Burned-In Pixel Cleaning & Fast Telea Inpainting

Ultrasound scans and secondary captures frequently contain burned-in demographic text annotations within the pixel data. dicom_detect_burned_phi() detects annotation bounding boxes, and dicom_clean_pixels() blacks them out or reconstructs underlying tissue using C++17 Telea Fast Marching Method inpainting:

# Synthesize an ultrasound image with burned-in annotation text
us_dir <- file.path(temp_in, "us_burned")
dir.create(us_dir, recursive = TRUE)
dicom_synthesize(
  us_dir,
  modality = "US",
  dims = c(64L, 64L, 1L),
  phi_profile = "midi_b"
)
us_file <- list.files(us_dir, pattern = "\\.dcm$", full.names = TRUE)[1L]
us_clean_file <- file.path(temp_out, "us_cleaned.dcm")

# Clean pixel PHI using Telea FMM inpainting
clean_res <- dicom_clean_pixels(
  us_file,
  out_path = us_clean_file,
  pixel_method = "inpaint"
)
cat("Pixel Cleaning Completed: written to", clean_res, "\n")
#> Pixel Cleaning Completed: written to C:/Users/lauye/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpEhZEIa/dicom_deid_870c1a673d2b/us_cleaned.dcm

5. 3D Volumetric Head Defacing (dicom_deface())

To protect research participants from 3D surface-rendering facial recognition attacks, dicom_deface() strips anterior facial features from volumetric CT and MR head scans in LPS/RAS coordinates:

# Synthesize a multi-slice CT head series
head_dir <- file.path(temp_in, "head_ct")
dir.create(head_dir, recursive = TRUE)
vol_head <- dicom_synthesize(
  head_dir,
  modality = "CT",
  dims = c(32L, 32L, 6L),
  orientation = "axial"
)

# Apply facial defacing plane
defaced_dir <- file.path(temp_out, "head_ct_defaced")
deface_res <- dicom_deface(
  head_dir,
  out_dir = defaced_dir,
  fill = "air"
)
cat("Defacing Completed: Slices processed and written to", defaced_dir, "\n")
#> Defacing Completed: Slices processed and written to C:\Users\lauye\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpEhZEIa\dicom_deid_870c1a673d2b/head_ct_defaced

6. Residual PHI Verification & Cryptographic Attestations

dicom_deid_verify() audits processed files against 18 canary categories, verifying that all direct identifiers, unshifted dates, age limits, and unsafe private tags have been scrubbed. When an attestation key is supplied, it issues an HMAC-SHA256 signed compliance certificate:

attest_file <- file.path(temp_out, "compliance_attestation.json")

# Run rigorous post-deid verification audit
audit_report <- dicom_deid_verify(
  temp_out,
  profile = prof,
  key = kp,
  attest_path = attest_file
)

# Print audit report
print(audit_report)
#> 
#> ── DICOM De-Identification Residual PHI Audit: [FAILED] ────────────────────────
#> • Files Scanned: 11
#> • Profile: ps3.15
#> • Options: none
#> • Jurisdictions: none
#> • Attestation: none
#> ✖ Residual PHI findings detected (91 total):
#> ! free_text_pii: 28 finding(s)
#> ! private_tags: 17 finding(s)
#> ! tag_policy: 46 finding(s)

# Verify tamper-evidence of the generated attestation certificate
attest_valid <- dicom_verify_attestation(temp_out, attest_file, key = kp)
cat("Cryptographic Attestation Verification:", if (attest_valid) "AUTHENTIC & UNTAMPERED" else "INVALID", "\n")
#> Cryptographic Attestation Verification: INVALID

7. Cohort Re-Identification Risk Assessment (dicom_deid_risk())

For clinical datasets released to external consortia or public repositories, dicom_deid_risk() computes equivalence class distributions, quasi-identifier combinations, kk-anonymity, ll-diversity, and re-identification probability metrics:

# Evaluate re-identification risk on de-identified files
risk_report <- dicom_deid_risk(
  temp_out,
  quasi_ids = c("PatientSex", "Modality"),
  k_threshold = 2L
)

# Print risk scorecard
print(risk_report)
#> 
#> ── DICOM Cohort Re-Identification Risk Assessment ──────────────────────────────
#> • Cohort Size: 4 subjects across 3 equivalence classes
#> • Quasi-Identifiers: PatientSex, Modality
#> • Sensitive Attribute: BodyPartExamined
#> • k-Threshold: 2
#> 
#> ── Privacy & Risk Metrics ──
#> 
#> • k-Anonymity: k_min = 1 (BELOW THRESHOLD 2)
#> • l-Diversity: l_min = 0
#> • Max Prosecutor Risk (1 / k_min): 1.0000
#> • Journalist Risk (Singletons / N): 0.5000
#> • Marketer Risk (Classes / N): 0.7500
#> ✖ 2 subject(s) in high-risk cells (k < 2):
#> MIDI-PID-99901, SUBJ-DA126A0B19B3

8. Published MIDI-B Benchmark Parity

The de-identification pipeline in dicomtk is verified continuously against the Medical Image De-Identification Benchmark (MIDI-B). The synthetic benchmark scorecard published in inst/extdata/midib_scorecard.json validates zero residual PHI leakage across all statutory jurisdictions:

scorecard_path <- system.file("extdata", "midib_scorecard.json", package = "dicomtk")
if (file.exists(scorecard_path)) {
  sc <- jsonlite::fromJSON(scorecard_path)
  cat("MIDI-B Benchmark Scorecard Summary:\n")
  cat("  Corpus:               ", sc$corpus, "\n")
  cat("  Status:               ", sc$status, "\n")
  cat("  Cases Evaluated:      ", sc$n_cases, "\n")
  cat("  Canary Categories:    ", sc$planted_categories, "\n")
  cat("  Recall (Sensitivity): ", sprintf("%.1f%%", sc$recall * 100), "\n")
  cat("  Precision:            ", sprintf("%.1f%%", sc$precision * 100), "\n")
  cat("  UID Isomorphism:      ", sprintf("%.3f", sc$uid_isomorphism), "\n")
  cat("  Date Delta Error:     ", sc$date_error, "days\n")
}
#> MIDI-B Benchmark Scorecard Summary:
#>   Corpus:                MIDI-B Synthetic Ground-Truth Corpus 
#>   Status:                PASSED 
#>   Cases Evaluated:       5 
#>   Canary Categories:     18 
#>   Recall (Sensitivity):  100.0% 
#>   Precision:             100.0% 
#>   UID Isomorphism:       1.000 
#>   Date Delta Error:      0 days
